text:
elaine: apac (aps1) queue depth for mosaic-8b just jumped — ~4k inflight, p95 latency creeping past 3s, low-priority jobs are getting evicted :warning:
elaine: seeing admission queue growth specifically for model=mosaic-8b, region=aps1, stepping up since 09:12 UTC
infra-bot: ALERT: queue_depth>3000 on pool=mosaic-8b-aps1, spillover triggered to fallback routing (ratio=0.15) — metrics: qlen=4123, p50=420ms, p95=3.2s, p99=6.8s
raj: thanks. did autoscaler kick? any preempt events?
sam: autoscaler did a partial scale at 09:05 (scaled +2), then hit GPU preempt window at 09:10 so pods dropped. looks like warmup lag + sustained arrival spike.
elaine: current traffic profile shows a big burst from a single customer (acme-corp) and many smaller tails. free-tier + canaries account for ~22% of arrivals.
raj: can we reduce concurrency or throttle free-tier to buy time? what's the impact if we shed canaries?
sam: we can flip admission policy to strict for free-tier in aps1: `rbac route set --region=aps1 --tier=free --admit=deny` (will drop queue admission for new free requests, 503)
ops-oncall: prefer soft-shedding first — reduce per-worker concurrency from 8->4 for mosaic-8b in aps1: `infractl patch pool mosaic-8b-aps1 --concurrency 4`
elaine: that should reduce backlog growth rate without full 503. any cost/latency tradeoffs?
raj: concurrency down will increase latency for admitted requests but reduces queuing; acceptable short-term. also let's enable model-variant fallback: route 20% of traffic to mosaic-4b-quantized in aps1.
sam: doing that now: `routerctl split-route --from=mosaic-8b --to=mosaic-4b-q8 --region=aps1 --percent=20`
infra-bot: ACTION: split-route applied, policy id=pol-7831. monitoring for 5m
elaine: also can we prioritize enterprise customers in admission? acme-corp is enterprise — we should avoid degrading them.
raj: add priority rule: enterprise > paid > free. `admitctl set-priority --region=aps1 --order enterprise,paid,free`
ops-oncall: starting targeted pod drains for non-critical pools to free GPUs for mosaic-8b hot shard — `kdrain mosaic-tta-noncritical-1`
elaine: heads-up: draining will cause short preempt churn; expect a small bump in 503s for background batch jobs.
sam: I recommend temporarily enabling extra reserved capacity if budget allows: we have 4 spare GPUs in apac-reserved that can be unpaused. cost ~ $0.6/hr per GPU but saves customer latency.
elaine: budget ok for emergency for next 3 hours. please unpause 4 GPUs and attach to mosaic-8b-aps1 pool.
raj: unpause done: `capacityctl unpause --pool apac-reserved --count 4`
infra-bot: capacity event: 4 GPUs attached to pool mosaic-8b-aps1, pool replicas +4.
ops-oncall: monitoring backlog — qlen dropped from 4.1k -> 900 in 6m after scale + routing tweaks. p95 back to ~1.1s.
elaine: nice. next steps: 1) keep free-tier soft-shed until normal qlen<200 for 10m, 2) investigate customer burst pattern and add rate limits for acme-corp bot traffic, 3) postmortem if preempt window + autoscaler got misaligned.
raj: I'll own postmortem. sam, can you take rate-limit rule for acme-corp?
sam: on it — adding a per-customer token-bucket: `ratelimitctl set --customer acme-corp --region aps1 --qps 15`
ops-oncall: creating an incident ticket and adding runbook steps. incident ID: INC-20260320-aps1-queue1
elaine: thanks all. keep channel for updates; if qlen spikes again escalate to oncall paging. :thumbsup:
